CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the classic Raman fingerprint of a para-disubstituted benzene: a pair of very strong bands at 831 / 816 cm⁻¹ (ring C-H out-of-plane “para” doublet), a very strong 1208 cm⁻¹ band (ring in-plane C-H bend), intense CH₃ symmetric bend at 1382 cm⁻¹ and CH₃/CH₂ deformation at 1451 cm⁻¹, together with aromatic C=C stretches at 1582–1622 cm⁻¹. High-frequency bands at 3022 and 3064 cm⁻¹ correspond to aromatic C–H stretches, while 2872 and 2929 cm⁻¹ come from alkyl C–H stretches.  
Among the candidates, only molecules 1, 4, 5, 9 possess an aromatic ring; of these, compound 1 (Cc1ccc(C)cc1, p-xylene) is the sole symmetric para-disubstituted benzene with two methyl groups, exactly matching the dominant 831/816 cm⁻¹ doublet and the strong CH₃ deformation pair (1382/1451 cm⁻¹) observed. The absence of additional functional-group bands (e.g., strong C=O, broad O–H, or C–O stretches) further supports a simple hydrocarbon like p-xylene over candidates containing carbonyl, hydroxyl, methoxy or epoxide groups.
